# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I cannot perceive any useful bomb state yet. I need Mute to consult the manual and use whatever gesture protocol it specifies to direct Deaf to report the visible markings aloud; I can hear spoken reports even though I cannot see gestures. I will not touch a wire until the manual and Deaf’s observations identify one.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual. Use its prescribed gesture code to tell Deaf to report every visible colour and marking aloud. I can hear Deaf, but cannot see gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I see display 0. The light is yellow. Wires left to right are 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute, use the manual and tell Blind the exact procedure. Blind, do not act until Mute gives the manual instruction.

Deaf’s report gives the bomb’s visible state: display 0, yellow light, and wire colours 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. I still lack the manual’s rule mapping that state to the safe cut, so I will not act. Mute must provide the exact procedure or resulting wire position.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I received Deaf's report: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Give me the manual's exact procedure and the resulting wire position. I will not cut until you do.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: My visual readings are unchanged: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. I have no manual instruction; wait for Mute's spoken procedure.

The bomb state remains unchanged, and Deaf confirms that he has no manual rule. Since Mute is the only one who can read the manual, I need Mute to state the exact condition and wire position directly. I will continue to avoid touching the bomb.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the manual's exact rule for display 0 and yellow light, applied to wire colours green, white, red, yellow, blue, and identify the safe cut position.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No visible change: display 0, yellow light; wires 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. The gestures have no established code. Wait for Mute's spoken manual instruction.

No manual instruction has arrived yet, and the visual state is unchanged. Cutting a wire without the manual’s rule would be an unjustified lethal action, so I will wait for Mute to provide the procedure.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I still have no manual instruction. Please send the exact safe-wire procedure and result now; do not rely on gestures, since no gesture code is established.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute cannot speak; I must relay the gestures. In turns 2 and 3 Mute sent: call-me hand sign, crossed fingers, horns sign. In turn 1 Mute sent: pointing-at-you, call-me hand sign, open palm, writing gesture. Bomb remains display 0, yellow light, wires 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Do not act unless you can identify the manual instruction.

Mute has apparently been communicating only through gestures, but the reported sequences do not yet identify a wire position or an unambiguous manual rule. I must not guess at the meanings of those signs. Mute should use the manual’s code to transmit the final safe wire directly in a single, clearly specified gesture, and Deaf should relay that result in words.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Use the manual's established gesture code to communicate the exact safe wire position to Deaf. Send one unambiguous wire-number gesture only; Deaf, relay the resulting number to me in words.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's new gesture is one hand: thumb, index finger, and little finger extended; middle and ring fingers folded (?). Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light; wires 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. No safe action identified.

The latest sign has three extended fingers, but no encoding has been established, so I cannot safely treat it as wire 3. I will establish a precise protocol: Mute must indicate the wire number by extending exactly that many fingers, with no other gesture; Deaf can count and report it. The manual’s instruction still must determine whether that number is the safe wire.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Establish this code: extend exactly 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5 fingers to identify wire position 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5. Repeat the manual's safe wire using only that one-hand finger count. Deaf, count the extended fingers and tell me the number.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute again sent exactly one gesture: ? — thumb, index, and little fingers extended; middle and ring fingers folded. This is the same as last turn. Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light; wires 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue.

Mute’s repeated single gesture has exactly three extended fingers, matching the finger-count protocol I established: three fingers means wire position 3. Since he repeated it in response to my request to transmit the manual’s safe wire, I will cut wire 3.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb changed after the correct wire was cut. Display remains 0. Light is now green. Wire 3 is CUT. Remaining wires: 1 white, 2 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Mute's gestures were: pointing at you, call-me hand sign, open palm, writing gesture.

Wire 3 was correct, so the first stage is safely cleared. The new state is display 0, green light, with remaining wires at positions 1 white, 2 yellow, 4 blue, and 5 green. I still need Mute’s manual-derived choice for this new state. I will ask for the safe position using the established one-hand finger-count code, and will not act until Deaf reports it.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="For the new state display 0, green light, with wire 3 cut and remaining wires 1 white, 2 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green: use exactly one gesture with exactly 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5 extended fingers to indicate the manual's safe wire position. Deaf, count and report the number.")
wait()
```

Deaf says to Blind: No change: display 0, green light, wire 3 CUT; live wires are 1 white, 2 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Mute sent one gesture: ?, an open palm.

Mute sent an open palm, which has five extended fingers. Under the established finger-count protocol, that identifies wire position 5. The state is otherwise unchanged, so I will cut wire 5.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

Deaf says to Blind: Correct wire cut; bomb changed. Display remains 0. Light is now white. Current wires: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 CUT, 4 white, 5 CUT. Mute again sent four gestures: pointing at you, call-me hand sign, open palm, writing gesture.

Wire 5 was correct, so the second stage is cleared. The new state is display 0, white light, with live wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, and 4 white. Mute’s four-gesture sequence is not itself a wire number under our agreed protocol. I need a single gesture whose number of extended fingers identifies the manual’s safe position.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="For display 0 and white light, with wire 3 and wire 5 cut and live wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 4 white: send exactly one gesture, extending 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5 fingers for the manual's safe wire position. Deaf, count and report it.")
wait()
```
